uses: Oat straw is the green top growth of the oat plant, cut before it flowers. Grieve counted oats among the nervines, herbs thought to steady and feed the nerves, and the EMA recognizes the green herb as a traditional remedy for mild stress and to help with sleep. The grain had its own folk uses: thin oat gruel was a gentle food for invalids and new mothers, and Culpeper applied oatmeal poultices to itchy skin and boiled it with vinegar to fade freckles and spots.
caution_pregnancy: Safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been established, and the EMA does not recommend medicinal oat herb then. Not enough is known; avoid medicinal amounts.
caution_medications: The EMA reports no known interactions with medicines.
caution_conditions: If you have coeliac disease, take care. Oats don't contain gluten themselves, but they are usually grown, processed and shipped alongside wheat, barley and rye and can pick up gluten; some people with coeliac disease react even to oats labeled gluten-free. The EMA advises caution because data on the protein content of oat herb preparations aren't available. It may make you drowsy enough to affect driving; if it does, don't drive or use machines. The EMA does not recommend it for children under 12, or for anyone allergic to it. Grieve warned against oat gruel when indigestion comes with stomach acidity.
caution_duration: If stress or sleep problems continue while you are using it, see a doctor or qualified practitioner.
caution_topical: None of our sources reports skin problems from oat poultices. Don't use it if you are allergic to oats.
garden_harvest_timing: Cut the green tops before the plant flowers, to use fresh or dried.
garden_water: Well-drained, moderately fertile soil; copes with wet better than many grains, but not with flooding
notes: An annual grass 2 to 4 feet tall, first domesticated in the Middle East. Home gardeners often sow it in fall as a winter cover crop that smothers weeds; give it at least ten weeks of cool weather. Its residue holds back seed germination, so wait at least three weeks after it dies down before sowing vegetables there. The grain must be cooked before eating. Culpeper gives oats no planet.
